items: Git is a version control tool, helping developers manage and collaborate on code changes.
GitHub is a platform that hosts Git repositories, providing a user-friendly interface for collaborating on projects and managing Git repositories in the cloud.
git clone: Copies a remote repository to your local machine, allowing you to work on the project locally. git clone <repository-url>
git add .: Stages all changes in the current directory (and its subdirectories) to be committed. git add .
git commit -m "commit message": Commits the staged changes to your local repository, with a descriptive message about the changes. git commit -m "Added feature X"
git push: Pushes your local commits to a remote repository (e.g., GitHub), making your changes available to others. git push
git pull: Fetches the latest changes from a remote repository and merges them into your local repository. git pull
GitHub is a platform that hosts Git repositories online, providing a convenient way to share, collaborate on, and manage repositories in a centralized location.
Git is the version control tool used to manage source code, track changes, and facilitate collaboration.
Clone a repository from GitHub: git clone https://github.com/user/repository.git
Make some changes to the project locally (edit files, add new ones).
Add the modified files to the staging area: git add .
Commit the changes with a message explaining the update: git commit -m "Implemented new feature"
Push the changes to the remote repository on GitHub: git push
If there are updates from others, pull the latest changes: git pull

content.text: Git helps keep track of code versions, collaborate with team members, and manage changes efficiently throughout a project.
